name: Clídna

attributes.attribute: Irish figure joined to bright-feathered birds
companions whose songs eased the pain of the sick
a goddess of great beauty tied to Co. Cork
drowned by the wave Tonn Chliodhna at Glandore
called the queen of the fairies of Munster

sources: Gregory, Lady Augusta. Gods and Fighting Men: The Story of the Tuatha De Danaan and of the Fianna of Ireland. New York: Oxford University Press, 1970.
Gwynn, Edward. The Metrical Dindshenchas. Vol. III. Royal Irish Academy, Todd Lecture Series. Dublin: Hodges, Figgis, and Co., Ltd., 1906–1924, 207–213.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Clídna, also spelled Cliodna, Cliodhna, Cliona, and Cleena, is the great Munster goddess of beauty. Tradition calls her the shapely one and ties her closely to Co. Cork. Some accounts name her the queen of the fairies of Munster. She stands as the counterpart of the goddesses Áine and Aibell. Her father is Gebann, the chief druid of Manannán mac Lir. She dwells in the otherworld realm Tír Tairngire when Ciabhán of the Fianna wins her love. He carries her to Ireland in his curragh and lands at Glandore harbour. While he hunts ashore, a great wave sweeps over the sleeping goddess and drowns her. That wave endures in Glandore harbour as Tonn Chliodhna, the wave of Clídna. Irish tradition counts the wave among its three great waves. A second account blames the harper Iuchna, whose music lulls her to sleep. The vision of Tadg mac Céin shows her kept by three bright birds. The birds feed on apples from an otherworld tree. Their songs bring healing sleep to the sick. Drowning does not end her story. She takes a line of mortal lovers, among them Earl Gerald FitzGerald and Caomh, ancestor of the O'Keeffes. Her power marks two rocks called Carrigcleena, one near Mallow and one off Ross Carbery. She serves the MacCarthy family as their fairy woman. Tradition credits her with revealing the secret of the Blarney Stone. Fenian tales later recast her as a daughter of Libra.

okr.objective: Clídna is the Munster goddess of beauty whose drowning wave Tonn Chliodhna still marks Glandore harbour.
key_results: Daughter of Gebann, druid of Manannán mac Lir, and love of Ciabhán.
Drowned at Glandore harbour by the wave remembered as Tonn Chliodhna.
Kept three bright birds whose songs healed the sick with sleep.
Took mortal lovers such as Earl Gerald FitzGerald and Caomh of the O'Keeffes.
